info.title: OpenAsy Calendar API
info.summary: Calendars and contacts on the company's own mail server: invitations, free and busy, rooms and sharing, on Stalwart.
info.description:
Every screen of Calendar uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Teams and rooms are set in calendar.yaml, never through the API; Calendar keeps the mail server in step with it. A person's own calendars, contacts and device passwords take the session of that person, never an API token. Everything else takes a session or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: user, viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when Calendar runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the Calendar origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_calendar_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when Calendar is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.
